title: Intel Secures Tesla Deal to Produce Next-Generation Chips
author: B
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Santa Clara, Monday, 19 October 2026.
Tesla has agreed to use Intel’s advanced 14A process, handing a crucial commercial win to Intel’s expanding contract manufacturing business as it targets profitability.

Tesla has agreed to use Intel’s advanced 14A process, handing a crucial commercial win to Intel’s expanding contract manufacturing business as it targets profitability [1][2]. Intel Corporation (NasdaqGS: INTC) announced this major milestone for its foundry business on October 17, 2026, marking a significant vote of confidence in its contract chip-making strategy [1]. The deal offers business leaders and investors a clear signal of shifting dynamics within the global semiconductor supply chain, particularly as Intel reports steady operational progress on output yields [1][2]. This agreement signifies external chip buyer interest in Intel’s advanced logic roadmap beyond legacy nodes, validating the company’s heavy investment in next-generation manufacturing capabilities [1].

Intel Foundry is currently operating with substantial financial headwinds, reporting operating losses of approximately US$2.5 billion per quarter [2]. To fund new factory buildouts for foundry expansion, Intel announced a US$20 billion equity raise, introducing narrative risk regarding potential impacts on free cash flow [1][2]. Analysts project that the Intel Foundry segment aims to reach operating breakeven by late 2028, a target that investors are closely monitoring alongside disclosure of additional named customers [1][2]. The current quarterly loss implies an annualized operational deficit of 10 billion, highlighting the scale of the challenge management faces to close the financial gap [2][3].

Despite the announcement, critical details regarding the Tesla agreement remain undisclosed, including production volume, execution timeline, and cost-sharing structures [3][4]. While Elon Musk stated that Tesla plans to use the 14A process for the Terafab project, some reports indicate that Tesla and other entities like SpaceX were still evaluating Intel’s manufacturing capabilities as of mid-October 2026 [3][5]. This uncertainty underscores the need for Intel to convert technological developments into verified commercial orders to justify the capital expenditure [3]. Investors are advised to monitor disclosures on 18A and 14A loading, as well as any shift in the operating loss trajectory throughout 2027 [2][4].

Beyond Tesla, analyst reports suggest Intel Foundry has reportedly secured or is exploring projects with Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Microsoft, and Broadcom [5]. The Intel 14A process, built around RibbonFET 2 and PowerDirect backside power delivery, is central to these opportunities as the company competes against TSMC for leading-edge foundry customers [5]. However, the clearest signal of success will be whether Intel starts disclosing meaningful dollar commitments as it funds new fabs with the US$20 billion raise [1][5]. If successful, Intel could strengthen its position as an alternative to TSMC and contribute to a more diversified global semiconductor supply chain [5].
